classification.difficultyReason: Expand products and select useful coefficient equations, then substitute between constraints. Part (c) requires using the linear coefficient to resolve the sign left by a squared parameter; part (d) requires extracting the specified coefficient. These are routine linked applications of the taught method.

content.prompt: Find the missing values by equating coefficients.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}4x^3+(x+a)(x+b)+cx&=4x^3+x^2+(a+b+c)x+ab\end{align*}$$
Equating coefficients of $x^3$:
$$\begin{align*}a-3&=4\\a&=7\end{align*}$$
Equating constant terms:
$$\begin{align*}7b&=-42\\b&=-6\end{align*}$$
Equating coefficients of $x$:
$$\begin{align*}7-6+c&=-1\\c&=-2\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}(x+5)(x+b)&=x^2+(b+5)x+5b\\(ax+1)(x+5)(x+b)&=ax^3+[a(b+5)+1]x^2+(5ab+b+5)x+5b\end{align*}$$
Equating coefficients of $x^3$ and constant terms:
$$\begin{align*}a&=2\\5b&=30\\b&=6\end{align*}$$
The remaining coefficients agree: $2(6+5)+1=23$ and $5(2)(6)+6+5=71$.

$$\begin{align*}(x+a)^2(x-2)&=(x^2+2ax+a^2)(x-2)\\&=x^3+(2a-2)x^2+(a^2-4a)x-2a^2\end{align*}$$
Equating constant terms:
$$\begin{align*}-2a^2&=-18\\a^2&=9\end{align*}$$
Equating coefficients of $x$:
$$\begin{align*}a^2-4a&=-3\\9-4a&=-3\\a&=3\end{align*}$$
Equating coefficients of $x^2$:
$$\begin{align*}b&=2(3)-2\\b&=4\end{align*}$$
